title: One Cube Estimate Implies the Yang–Mills Mass Gap
description: Source, programs and Lean 4 certificate of the paper One Cube Estimate Implies the Yang–Mills Mass Gap, by Deep Bhattacharjee, Ushashi Bhattacharya, James Montgomery Lockwood and Tristan Romanov (Hexagon preprint 2610.00341). The gauge of four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory is fixed on a period-two field of straight lines that meets every plaquette in exactly one link. At fixed lattice spacing this gives a unique free-boundary state, reflection positivity, exponential clustering and an explicit transfer-matrix gap: for SU(2) up to beta_W = 0.348 through plaquette blocks with constants proved by hand, and for SU(3) up to beta_W = 0.52 through plaquette blocks with constants proved by hand, and for every compact simple group G when N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/29, with kappa_G the least Ricci curvature. A Dobrushin–Shlosman condition on one cube of fixed physical size, uniform along the continuum tuning, gives a mass gap in physical units in every continuum limit, also for observables smoothed by the gradient flow; the paper proves what that cube estimate needs and which Osterwalder–Schrader properties a limit of the flowed fields has. Towards the estimate it labels the blocks of Balaban's averages, proves that the weight of bad islands factorises through kernels on the good layers between them with cross-ratios exponentially small in the widths of the layers, gives the explicit coupling past which bad islands and their clusters are rarer than their entropy, and controls one step of the block map on the large fields and on the calm small fields. It also reduces the cube estimate to an averaged condition, proves that this condition descends to block variables and climbs one scale under a split inequality, proves that inequality at strong coupling and on each finite torus, reduces the condition at the coarsest scale to Dobrushin bounds on the single-link coefficients of the laws of the block variables, which one step of the block map contracts and which gauge covariance excludes at weak coupling, proves for SU(2) that the block variables approach the Haar measure as the coupling is tuned, which gives the condition at the coarsest scale on tori of side up to exp(2^k/(17k)) after k blocking steps, proves that site-additive metrics on the block variables lose a fixed factor at every scale at which the reconstruction changes sign, which the conditional means of block averages always do, while metrics with a term for the deviation from the reconstructed field compose with a loss independent of the number of scales once one two-term inequality holds at every scale, and states the conditional chain for every compact simple group. Lean 4 (Mathlib) checks the combinatorics of the line field and the block gauge, the finite arithmetic of the perturbation propositions and the chain of rational bounds of the SU(2) blocks; the ball-arithmetic programs (python-flint), which no proof uses, are included. The averaged covariance of the labels, the effective action across all scales and a nontrivial continuum limit are not proved; the Clay Millennium problem is open. The archive also keeps the sources of two earlier papers of the project in tex/ and strong-coupling/prd/.
